observations.observed: Three black-and-white apparatus scenes: upper left, upper right, and lower center. Printed scene letters appear as a, Cyrillic be, and Cyrillic ve. Each scene has an adjustable bellows/cylinder apparatus, a flexible connecting hose, and a round gauge on a support.

The bellows is held between upper and lower plates with side supports and a vertical screw/handle. A vertical graduated strip is beside it. A hose runs from the apparatus toward the round gauge to its right. A slender slanted thermometer-like instrument lies outside the apparatus below the hose. The gauge has a circular rim, many short marks, tiny glyphs, a central hub and a pointer extending toward the upper right.

The bellows and screw are inside an open cylindrical bath vessel on a rectangular support block. A slanted slender thermometer passes into the bath at the left. A graduated strip is beside the bellows. The screw projects high above the vessel. A hose curves rightward/downward to a round gauge on a support; its pointer extends toward the upper right.

A second bath-mounted apparatus has the same identifiable vessel, block, thermometer, graduated strip, screw/handle, hose and gauge roles. The bellows appears shorter/compressed compared with the upper-right bath scene. The gauge pointer extends toward the lower right; the opposite short portion is visible toward the upper left.

sourceRelationships: Each hose visually joins its apparatus outlet to the corresponding gauge connection.
Each screw aligns with the bellows/upper plate in its own apparatus.
The bath scenes place their bellows inside the vessel and their thermometer into the vessel.
Each bath vessel rests above its corresponding rectangular block.
Gauge marks and pointer are contained within their corresponding circular dial.
The three printed scene labels sit outside the apparatus, beneath their own scenes.
